title: Theft
summary: Dishonestly taking movable property out of someone's possession without consent. Covers stolen phones, wallets, bikes, vehicles, jewellery and cash.
keywords: theft stole stolen steal missing taken phone mobile wallet purse bike scooter car vehicle cash jewellery laptop pickpocket

old_law: No direct IPC equivalent (earlier treated as theft/robbery)
title: Snatching
summary: Theft where the offender suddenly or quickly seizes or grabs movable property from a person, like a chain or phone snatched on the road.
keywords: snatch snatched snatching grabbed chain necklace phone bike riders road street ran away

title: Theft in a dwelling house, transport or place of worship
summary: Theft committed inside a house, building used as a dwelling, means of transport or place of worship. Often applies to home burglaries along with house trespass.
keywords: house home flat room burglary broke break-in thief entered stolen almirah locker temple bus train

title: Extortion
summary: Intentionally putting someone in fear of injury to dishonestly make them hand over money, property or valuable security. Includes threats to leak photos unless paid.
keywords: extortion threaten pay money demand blackmail leak photos video unless ransom hafta

title: Robbery
summary: Theft or extortion where the offender causes or attempts to cause death, hurt or wrongful restraint, or fear of it. For example being stopped and forced to hand over valuables.
keywords: robbery robbed knife gun weapon forced hand over looted attacked took money threatened

title: Dishonest misappropriation of property
summary: Dishonestly misappropriating or converting someone else's movable property to one's own use, for example keeping property found or given by mistake.
keywords: misappropriation kept refused return found property mistake belongings

title: Criminal breach of trust
summary: Someone entrusted with property or money dishonestly uses or keeps it against the terms of the trust. Common in disputes with business partners, employers, agents or relatives holding money.
keywords: breach trust entrusted gave money partner employer agent misused not returned deposit kept jewellery stridhan

title: Stolen property
summary: Dishonestly receiving or keeping property knowing or having reason to believe it is stolen.
keywords: stolen property receiving buying selling second-hand found my stolen phone

title: Cheating
summary: Deceiving someone to dishonestly make them deliver property or money, or do something they would not otherwise do. Covers many frauds, fake job offers, fake sellers and investment scams.
keywords: cheating cheated fraud scam fake deceived lied paid money advance job offer investment online seller never delivered refund 420

title: Cheating by personation
summary: Cheating by pretending to be some other person, for example a caller pretending to be a bank officer, police officer or relative.
keywords: personation pretending pretended impersonation posed as bank officer police officer customs relative fake identity caller

title: Mischief
summary: Intentionally destroying or damaging property to cause wrongful loss or damage, like breaking a vehicle's glass or damaging a shop.
keywords: mischief damage damaged broke vandalised destroyed property car glass shop door fire

title: Criminal trespass and house trespass
summary: Entering or staying on someone's property with intent to commit an offence, intimidate, insult or annoy. House trespass is when this happens in a dwelling.
keywords: trespass entered house land plot property without permission forcefully occupied broke in neighbour

title: Forgery
summary: Making a false document or electronic record with intent to cause damage, support a false claim or commit fraud, like a forged signature or fake property papers.
keywords: forgery forged signature fake document papers property deed certificate false record

title: Criminal intimidation
summary: Threatening someone with injury to their body, reputation or property to cause alarm or make them do or not do something. Threats can be in person, by phone or messages.
keywords: threat threatened threatening intimidation kill harm messages calls warned scared fear life

title: Intentional insult to provoke breach of peace
summary: Intentionally insulting someone in a way meant to provoke them to break the peace or commit an offence, such as abusive language in a quarrel.
keywords: abuse abused abusive language insult gaali quarrel fight provoke neighbour

title: Defamation
summary: Making or publishing false imputations about a person intending to harm their reputation, in words, signs or posts. There are exceptions, like truth for public good.
keywords: defamation reputation false allegations posted social media spreading rumours lies about me

title: Voluntarily causing hurt
summary: Intentionally causing bodily pain, disease or infirmity to someone, like slapping, punching or beating.
keywords: hit beat beaten slapped punched kicked hurt injured attack assault fight pain bruise

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
summary: Causing serious injuries such as fractures, loss of sight or hearing, permanent disfigurement, or injuries that endanger life or cause severe pain for a long time.
keywords: grievous fracture broken bone serious injury hospital stitches eye teeth permanent

title: Hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
summary: Causing hurt or grievous hurt using a weapon, sharp object, fire, poison, corrosive substance or other dangerous means.
keywords: knife rod stick weapon blade stabbed attacked with dangerous burn

title: Attempt to murder
summary: Doing an act with intention or knowledge that it could cause death, where death does not happen.
keywords: attempt murder tried to kill strangled shot stabbed nearly died

title: Causing death by negligence (including hit and run)
summary: Causing death by a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, such as rash driving or medical negligence. A stricter part covers drivers who escape without reporting.
keywords: accident death died negligence rash driving hit and run truck car ran over doctor negligence

title: Wrongful restraint and wrongful confinement
summary: Obstructing someone from going where they have a right to go, or confining them within limits, like locking someone in a room or not letting them leave.
keywords: locked room confined not allowed leave stopped blocked restrained held captive

title: Kidnapping
summary: Taking or enticing a minor, or a person of unsound mind, out of the keeping of their lawful guardian without consent, or taking a person out of India without consent.
keywords: kidnapping kidnapped child minor missing daughter son taken away guardian

title: Assault or criminal force on a woman to outrage her modesty
summary: Using force or assaulting a woman intending to, or knowing it is likely to, outrage her modesty, such as groping or touching inappropriately.
keywords: woman molested molestation touched groped inappropriately modesty bus crowd

title: Sexual harassment
summary: Unwelcome physical contact and advances, demand for sexual favours, showing pornography against a woman's will, or sexually coloured remarks.
keywords: sexual harassment harassed remarks advances boss colleague workplace favours lewd comments

title: Voyeurism
summary: Watching or capturing images of a woman in a private act where she expects not to be observed, or sharing such images.
keywords: voyeurism hidden camera recorded secretly bathroom changing room private video

title: Stalking
summary: Repeatedly following or contacting a woman despite clear disinterest, or monitoring her use of the internet, email or other electronic communication.
keywords: stalking stalker following follows me repeatedly calls messages ex boyfriend tracking instagram

title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman
summary: Saying words, making sounds or gestures, or showing objects intending to insult a woman's modesty, including eve-teasing.
keywords: eve teasing whistling comments gestures obscene insult woman modesty street

title: Rape
summary: Defines rape and its punishment. Survivors can report at any police station, get free medical treatment at any hospital, and have their statement recorded by a woman officer.
keywords: rape sexual assault forced sex raped consent survivor

title: Cruelty by husband or his relatives
summary: A husband or his relatives subjecting a woman to cruelty, meaning conduct likely to drive her to harm herself or harassment to meet unlawful demands like dowry.
keywords: husband in-laws mother-in-law cruelty domestic violence wife married beaten harassed dowry marital home

title: Dowry death
summary: Death of a woman by burns, bodily injury or unnatural circumstances within seven years of marriage, where she faced cruelty or harassment for dowry soon before death.
keywords: dowry death died married sister daughter in-laws unnatural burns suspicious

title: Giving, taking or demanding dowry
summary: Giving or taking dowry, and directly or indirectly demanding dowry from the bride's parents or relatives, are offences.
keywords: dowry demand demanded money car gold marriage wedding in-laws

title: Identity theft
summary: Fraudulently or dishonestly using someone else's electronic signature, password or other unique identification feature, like a hacked account or misused OTP.
keywords: identity theft hacked account password otp aadhaar misused login profile email whatsapp hacked

title: Cheating by personation using a computer resource
summary: Cheating someone by pretending to be another person using a phone, computer or online platform. Covers most online and UPI frauds, fake customer care and digital arrest scams.
keywords: online fraud upi cyber scam fake customer care call link otp bank account debited digital arrest video call courier kyc

title: Violation of privacy (private images)
summary: Intentionally capturing, publishing or transmitting images of a person's private area without consent.
keywords: private photos images shared without consent leaked intimate pictures morphed

title: Publishing obscene or sexually explicit material electronically
summary: Publishing or transmitting obscene or sexually explicit material online, for example circulating a person's morphed or explicit photos or videos.
keywords: obscene explicit video posted online circulated morphed photos social media whatsapp group

act: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Sexual offences against children and duty to report
summary: Covers sexual assault and sexual harassment of anyone under 18. Anyone who knows of such an offence should report it to the police or Special Juvenile Police Unit.
keywords: child minor under 18 school teacher touched sexual abuse niece daughter son boy girl pocso

title: FIR for cognizable offences (including Zero FIR and e-FIR)
summary: Information about a cognizable offence can be given to any police station, orally or electronically, and must be recorded, even if the crime happened in another area (Zero FIR). The informant should get a free copy of the FIR.
keywords: fir police station complaint report file register zero fir e-fir online copy

title: If police refuse to register an FIR
summary: If the officer in charge refuses to record information, the person can send the substance of it in writing or by post to the Superintendent of Police, and can also approach the Magistrate.
keywords: police refused not registering fir won't file ignored superintendent sp complaint written

title: Non-cognizable offences (NC report)
summary: For non-cognizable offences, police record the information and refer the person to the Magistrate. Police cannot investigate without the Magistrate's order.
keywords: non-cognizable nc complaint police said minor matter magistrate permission

title: Magistrate ordering investigation
summary: A Magistrate can order the police to investigate a cognizable offence on an application, usually after the complainant has first approached the police and SP.
keywords: magistrate order investigation police not acting court application refused fir

title: Private complaint to a Magistrate
summary: A person can file a complaint directly before a Magistrate, who examines the complainant and witnesses before deciding whether to proceed.
keywords: private complaint magistrate court directly case file court

title: Statements to police and to a Magistrate
summary: Police may record statements of witnesses during investigation. A Magistrate can record statements and confessions, which is common for victims of sexual offences.
keywords: statement witness recorded police investigation magistrate victim statement

title: Police report after investigation (chargesheet)
summary: After investigation, police send a final report to the Magistrate. The informant should be told about the progress of the investigation.
keywords: chargesheet charge sheet final report investigation status progress closure

title: Arrest without warrant and notice of appearance
summary: Sets when police can arrest without a warrant. For many offences police must first issue a notice asking the person to appear instead of arresting.
keywords: arrest arrested police picked up warrant notice appear custody detained

title: Bail and anticipatory bail
summary: Bail is a right in bailable offences and at the court's discretion in non-bailable ones. A person fearing arrest can apply for anticipatory bail to the Sessions Court or High Court.
keywords: bail anticipatory bail fear arrest false case accused jail custody released

title: Electronic records as evidence
summary: Electronic records like screenshots, call recordings, CCTV footage and chats can be used as evidence, usually with a certificate about how they were produced.
keywords: screenshots evidence chats whatsapp call recording cctv video email proof electronic

title: Who can get free legal aid
summary: Women, children, SC/ST members, victims of trafficking, people with disabilities, people in custody, and people below the income limit can get a free lawyer through Legal Services Authorities.
keywords: free lawyer legal aid cannot afford poor money advocate help nalsa dlsa

title: Reporting cyber fraud quickly
summary: For online money fraud, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in as soon as possible, since quick reporting can help freeze the money. Keep transaction IDs and screenshots.
keywords: cyber online fraud upi money debited bank scam hacked 1930 report portal
